source.title: When Does ℓ2-Boosting Overfit Benignly? High-Dimensional Risk Asymptotics and the ℓ1 Implicit Bias
source.authors: Ye Su; Jian Li; Yong Liu

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It analyzes risk across feature-dimension ratios and boosting time, testing general double-descent and epoch-wise claims with ℓ1 interpolation and continuous-time boosting rather than the original deep-network settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own theoretical risk results and empirical risk trajectories, which are recorded below. Cited findings from other work are not recorded. The maximum-weight noise-localization measurement is not a test of the listed risk-curve versions.
record.test_reason: The paper never frames itself as a double-descent study. It is a benign-overfitting analysis. Still, its own theory and simulations report how interpolating risk changes as the feature-to-sample ratio grows past the interpolation threshold (γ>1), for ℓ1/Basis Pursuit, ℓ2 min-norm and XGBoost. That bears on the second-descent part of V4 in a new model class. It also shows one test-risk path over continuous boosting time, which bears weakly on V2. All risk results are pure-noise variance (β*=0), except the boosting-path experiment.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that ℓ1 implicit bias localizes noise, giving Θ(σ²/log(p/n)) variance decay under isotropic designs (Θ(σ²) at fixed proportional γ). Spiked-isotropic designs with r2≫n let risk vanish, but only at Θ(σ²/log(r2/n)), slower than ℓ2. An analytical noise-floor early stopping rule intercepts the overfitting rebound. Under a bounded ℓ1-path condition it attains minimax prediction rates and matches LassoCV and 5-fold CV.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes continuous-time ℓ2-Boosting and Basis Pursuit via high-dimensional CGMT risk asymptotics, with numerical illustrations and an exploratory XGBoost experiment. It does not reproduce the original deep-network model-size, epoch, or sample-size sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: Risk behavior depends on covariance setting: isotropic designs retain Θ(σ²) risk at a fixed finite p/n ratio, while spiked-isotropic designs have a declining regime when the isotropic tail ratio exceeds 1. The temporal trajectory depends on stopping time; the reported test risk rebounds after its minimum.

fits_no_version.finding: The maximum feature weight ‖β̂‖∞ of ℓ1 interpolants stays around 0.1 as γ grows, while for ℓ2 it decays toward zero (Fig 1c).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The ℓ1/greedy implicit bias localizes interpolated noise into a sparse active set, slowing post-threshold variance decay.

record.problems: The main theoretical results concern fixed-dictionary ℓ1 interpolation rather than deep networks. Empirical runs use moderate sample sizes (up to n = 800); risk values are mostly plotted rather than tabulated. The XGBoost result is described as exploratory and the paper notes that adaptive-tree theory remains open.
record.rows_left_out: No additional risk-curve findings bearing on the tested versions were left out. The study's maximum-feature-weight localization result was not included as a risk-curve row.

untested.parts: The first descent / classical U-shaped under-parameterized region. A test-error peak with signal present. Deep networks and other model classes beyond ℓ1/ℓ2 linear interpolants and XGBoost.
Epoch-wise behavior for larger p/n ratios, noisy-label classification, or deep networks. Only one boosting-path configuration is shown.
Untested: no peak-vs-noise sweep, no multiple descent, no optimally tuned regularization sweep. Early stopping is studied only as a stopping rule.

missing.what: Universality experiment: ℓ1 interpolant pure-noise excess variance versus γ∈[2,30] (n=800) for Gaussian, Rademacher and Student-t(4) designs. Variance decreases with γ and the curves overlap; 1/log fits give R²=0.9999, 0.9991 and 0.9995.
ℓ2 min-norm baseline under the isotropic design, decaying rapidly toward zero with γ.

record.verdict_notes: The paper frames everything as benign overfitting, not double descent. Risk curves are pure-noise variance only, so no full test-error double-descent curve with signal is shown. The spiked-isotropic figure shows elevated variance for γ<1 and decay for γ>1, but no explicit peak value is reported. Most values are figure-only. Tranche changed from T2 to T3, since this is a new model class with a result on the post-threshold descent rather than a different method aimed at the original question.

versions.untested_parts: Deep-network model-wise test-error double descent as model size grows.
The study tests continuous-time ℓ2-Boosting, not other architectures or discrete training procedures.
No increase in training-sample count near an interpolation threshold is tested.
The study tests risk against feature dimension or tail-dimension ratios in ℓ1 interpolation and an exploratory XGBoost setting, not across all model classes or the full classical U-shaped curve.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as predicting peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.
The study analyzes pure-noise risk and early stopping, but does not test whether noise drives a double-descent peak, multiple peaks, or disappearance under optimally tuned regularization.
No re-counting of complexity by effective parameters is tested.

rows.subject: Basis Pursuit interpolant (ℓ2-Boosting late-stopping limit)
rows.size_stated: p features and n samples; p/n → ∞
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical risk analysis as the feature-to-sample ratio grows under isotropic Gaussian pure noise.
rows.baseline: For the ℓ2 minimum-norm interpolant, the text states a variance component of order O(σ² n/p).
rows.note: The text states that risk decays as the feature-to-sample ratio diverges, but more slowly than in ℓ2 geometry.

rows.subject: Basis Pursuit interpolant (ℓ2-Boosting late-stopping limit)
rows.size_stated: p features and n samples; p/n → γ ∈ (1, ∞)
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical risk analysis in the fixed proportional regime under isotropic designs.
rows.value: Θ(σ²), i.e. it does not decay with sample size
rows.note: This qualifies the benign-risk result: at any fixed proportional ratio above 1, the risk does not vanish with sample size.
rows.check: Remark 4.2 concerns non-vanishing risk as n→∞ at a fixed ratio γ. That is a benign-overfitting consistency question, not risk changing with capacity. It cannot show whether risk improves past the interpolation point, and Fig 1 shows risk still falling with γ.

rows.subject: Basis Pursuit interpolant (ℓ2-Boosting late-stopping limit)
rows.size_stated: tail dimension r2 = p − k*; k* = o(n)
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical risk analysis as isotropic tail dimension grows relative to sample size.
rows.baseline: For the ℓ2 minimum-norm interpolant, the text states tail variance decays at Θ(n/r2).
rows.value: Tail component Θ(σ² / log(r2/n)); total risk is asymptotically dominated by this component, with head component O(σ² k*/n).
rows.note: Risk tends to zero beyond the tail interpolation threshold, with logarithmic rather than linear attenuation.

rows.subject: ℓ1 interpolant (Basis Pursuit)
rows.size_stated: n = 800 for the rate regression; n ∈ {100, 200, 400, 800} in the finite-size comparison; γ = p/n ∈ [2, 30]
rows.operation_detail: Empirical risk measured over feature-to-sample ratios under isotropic Gaussian pure noise.
rows.measure: Excess variance/risk as a function of γ; OLS fit against 1/log(p/n)
rows.baseline: Minimum ℓ2-norm interpolant included as a comparative baseline; its excess variance is described as decaying rapidly toward zero.
rows.value: Risk described as decaying more slowly and remaining substantially elevated; OLS fit against 1/log(p/n) has R² = 0.9997 in the figure caption.
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviations/error bars over 20 trials are reported; numerical error-bar values not stated.
rows.note: The risk values are plotted rather than tabulated. The main text describes the slow decay and the figure caption reports the fit statistic.
rows.check: Minor: the text and caption give R²=0.9997, but the Fig 1b legend shows 0.9999. Pure-noise variance only.

source_check.problem: Source inconsistency: caption and prose report R²=0.9997; Figure 1b legend reports 0.9999.

rows.measure: Excess variance/risk as a function of tail ratio γ
rows.baseline: Minimum ℓ2-norm interpolants are included; their variance attenuation is described as strictly faster.
rows.value: Risk is described as elevated for γ < 1 and decaying for γ > 1; the overparameterized-region fit against 1/log((p − k*)/n) has R² = 0.9933 in the text and R² = 0.9959 in the Figure 3 caption.
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviations/error bars are reported; numerical error-bar values not stated.
rows.note: The text describes a transition at γ = 1 and subsequent logarithmic decay. The text and caption give different R² values; both are preserved.

rows.subject: Continuous-time ℓ2-Boosting flow
rows.operation_detail: Tracked out-of-sample excess test risk over the continuous boosting path.

conditions.value: s = 5 nonzero components, each of magnitude 3.0
analytical noise-threshold stopping rule; late-stopping limit also shown

rows.measure: Excess test risk over training time
rows.baseline: LassoCV optimum risk and 5-fold cross-validation stopping are shown as empirical baselines.
rows.value: The text describes a U-shaped curve: risk first decreases, then inflates during the overfitting rebound toward the late-stopping limit; a subsequent decline is not reported.
rows.note: The text explicitly characterizes a fall followed by a rebound, not the full fall-rise-fall pattern.
rows.check: Only the fall-then-rise toward the late-stopping (interpolation) limit is shown. No second descent over training time appears. This is one setting (n=800, p=1600, s=5), described from a figure only.

relationships.condition: ℓ1 implicit bias (Basis Pursuit / ℓ2-Boosting limit) and greedy XGBoost versus ℓ2 interpolation
relationships.reason: Under ℓ1 geometry the post-threshold improvement is only logarithmic, Θ(σ²/log(p/n)), versus Θ(n/p) for ℓ2. It needs exponentially more overparameterization, and XGBoost risk stays elevated (r01, r03, r04, r05, r08).
relationships.display_finding: Post-threshold improvement scaled as Θ(σ²/log(p/n)) under ℓ1 geometry versus Θ(n/p) under ℓ2, requiring exponentially more overparameterization; XGBoost risk remained elevated.

statements.correction: Basis Pursuit risk decreases logarithmically beyond interpolation; ℓ2 attenuation is faster. These results support V4's post-interpolation improvement in the tested settings.
statements.problem: The estimator-geometry comparison is accurate, but slower post-threshold improvement does not itself limit V4, which specifies no improvement rate.
